title: The Garou in the Dark Medieval
summary: Werewolves of the thirteenth century: a race apart, sworn to Gaia, hidden from humankind.

claims.text: Werewolves are born, never made: neither a bite nor a curse turns a human or wolf into one.
A Garou heals far faster than any beast, can smash an oak door, and a mail shirt will not stop its claws.
Spirits teach the Garou their Gifts, and every Garou owes a sacred duty to protect Gaia.
The Garou hide because humans vastly outnumber them and open war would likely wipe them out.

title: What Mortals Believe of Werewolves
summary: The rumours of the age, and how little of them is true.

claims.text: Most people take werewolves for sorcerers who sold their souls to Satan, or for humans changed by some means.
Supposed ways to become one include a bite, drinking from a wolf's paw print, wolfsbane or belladonna, or birth under an eclipse.
Of the common protections, only silver truly works; wolfsbane and the crucifix do not.
Werewolves do not serve Satan and do not acknowledge the Devil; their faith is thousands of years older than Christianity.
Werewolves are mortal: luck, skill or persistence can kill one.

title: Silver
summary: The lunar metal, the bane most feared by the Garou.

claims.text: Silver burns werewolves and they have little defence against it; one silver arrowhead can kill.
Few humans know of the weakness, and those who do can rarely afford enough silver for a weapon.

title: The Impergium Remembered
summary: The ancient culling of humans, and the regret it leaves.

claims.text: Thousands of years ago the Garou culled human numbers, until the gentler werewolves ended the practice.
Factions in almost every tribe call ending it the worst mistake the Garou ever made, but humans are now too many and too settled to begin again.
The Children of Gaia hold the Impergium itself to be the greatest failure of the Garou.

title: Why the Garou Do Not Raze the Cities
summary: What holds the werewolves back from war on humankind.

claims.text: Several tribes, the Children of Gaia, Bone Gnawers and Warders of Men above all, would fight such a war with all their strength.
Vampires love the cities and would likely side with humanity.
In open war humans would sooner or later learn the truth about silver.

title: The Eclipse of 1230
summary: In May 1230 a great eclipse stirs dread across the Garou Nation.

claims.text: In May of 1230 an eclipse darkens the sky so deeply that workers go home thinking night has come.
The Garou recall the Prophecies of Shadow, one of which came true when Constantinople fell.
The Ten Tribes fear their own prophecy will be next; the mood is a calm before a storm.

title: The Prophecies of Shadow
summary: A cryptic forecast of calamity, first given to a Red Talon.

claims.text: The Prophecies of Shadow were first given to a Red Talon.
The Red Talons have pressed hardest to spread word of the visions to the other tribes.

title: Werewolf Faith
summary: The Garou live beside the spirits and need no faith to believe in them.

claims.text: A Garou questions Gaia and the spirits no more than breathing; even one raised in a church cannot deny the living spirit of the world.
A werewolf who blends Garou truth with a human religion would be called a heretic in this age.
Without Gaia a Garou would lose the Gifts, leave werewolf society and sink into Harano, a slow wasting despair.
Some Garou make war on the Church and the papal knightly orders; others wait for the age to pass.
The Fenrir punish Odin-worship among their people, and in Poland the Shadow Lords curse the name Kupala.

title: Harano
summary: The great despair that takes a Garou cut off from Gaia.

claims.text: A Garou without Gaia slides into Harano and wastes away alone and in pain.

title: Kinfolk
summary: Humans and wolves with werewolf blood, through whom the Garou breed.

claims.text: Garou must breed with Kinfolk to reproduce.
A tribe's human Kin usually live in one town or village near a caern; wolf Kin often range nearby.

title: Homid, Lupus and Metis
summary: Breeds in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: Homids are often more tolerant of humanity, though even they agree humans must be shielded from their own ignorance.
Lupus are raised in wolf packs; their first frenzies are shorter and less wild, but they have no inborn respect for humans.
The few metis allowed to live grow up among the Garou, better prepared than any homid or lupus, yet scorned for life.

title: Auspices
summary: The five moons of birth and the roles they bring.

claims.text: Ragabash, the tricksters, have little Rage but learn Gifts of misdirection and stealth.
Theurges, of the crescent moon, walk the spirit paths, guard against others' magic and most know healing.
The Philodox of the half moon are judges and lawgivers who can command spirits.
Galliards of the gibbous moon keep the histories and often open the sacred rites with dance and song.
Ahroun of the full moon are spirit warriors, the embodiment of Gaia's Rage.

title: The First Change
summary: How a cub becomes a werewolf, and how the sept brings the cub home.

claims.text: The First Change comes at puberty, usually under stress, and the new werewolf usually flies into frenzy.
Spirits and Kinfolk reach the local Garou near the time, and several werewolves come to fetch the cub.
Some septs force the Change by hunting and terrifying a cub on the full moon, which gave rise to the tale that a bite spreads lycanthropy.
After the Change, the cub is brought to a caern.

title: Black Furies
summary: A tribe of the Garou in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: The only all-female tribe, tracing descent from the Amazons; male children are exposed or given to other tribes.
They are strong in the Middle East and Byzantium and guard the females of every species.
Their totem is Pegasus.

title: Bone Gnawers
summary: A tribe of the Garou in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: Survivors tied to the lower classes and the growing urban poor, with little time for nobility.
With the Warders they even keep caerns inside human settlements.
Their totem is Rat.

title: Children of Gaia
summary: A tribe of the Garou in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: The peacemakers, who long for the days when all tribes were one and seek peaceful ways to hold back the Wyrm.
They rarely turn other tribes away from their caerns, yet fight fiercely when pushed too far.
Their totem is Unicorn.

title: Fenrir
summary: A tribe of the Garou in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: The harsh northern tribe steeped in Norse ways, who prize deeds over politics.
They read weakness in other tribes as a sign of possible taint.
Their totem is Fenris.

title: Fianna
summary: A tribe of the Garou in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: Spread with their Celtic kin, strongest in the British Isles, passionate in love and war.
Even the Silver Fangs defer to their lore of history; others fear their ties to the fae.
Their totem is Stag.

title: Red Talons
summary: A tribe of the Garou in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: The wolf tribe, still watchful of any human who enters their lands.
They have pressed the Prophecies of Shadow on the other tribes.
Their totem is Griffin.

title: Silent Striders
summary: A tribe of the Garou in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: Jackal-like wandering nomads who carry word between the closed septs of Europe.
Their Iberian Kin stand on both sides of the Reconquista war.
Their totem is Owl.

title: Silver Fangs
summary: A tribe of the Garou in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: The self-styled rulers and nobles of the Garou, now in slow decline.
Their Kin marry into Europe's noble houses, and other tribes whisper of madness among them.
Their totem is Falcon.

title: Shadow Lords
summary: A tribe of the Garou in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: A menacing tribe that means to replace the Silver Fangs as rulers.
Rumour says they deal with Leeches; they hold that the ends justify the means.
Their totem is Grandfather Thunder.

title: Warders of Men
summary: A tribe of the Garou in the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: The tribe closest to humans, at home in cities, above all the Italian city-states.
They study industry and invention, and some say they favour the Weaver over the Wyld.
Their totem is Cockroach.

title: The Ten Tribes
summary: The tribes of the Dark Medieval Garou, each under its own totem.

claims.text: Galliards sing that all Garou were once one tribe; now there are many, and wars between them are not rare.
Some tribes are tied to human peoples, like the Fenrir and Fianna; others cross borders, like the Bone Gnawers and Warders.
Each tribe honours its own totem spirit, which sets rules and teaches the tribe's Gifts.
The Garou of 1230 count Ten Tribes.

title: The Fall of the White Howlers
summary: How a Pictish tribe became the Black Spiral Dancers.

claims.text: The White Howlers were a great tribe living among Pictish Kin.
On the darkest night of Gaia's protectors the whole tribe went into a Wyrm pit, and none came back as they went in.
What climbed out were the Black Spiral Dancers, children of the Wyrm.
The Fianna still feel the loss of the White Howlers keenly.

title: Black Spiral Dancers
summary: Wyrm-worshipping Garou of the fouled caerns and the deep labyrinths.

claims.text: They worship the Wyrm from despoiled caerns.
Their deep labyrinths wind between the Umbra and the physical world; humans reach only dead ends.

title: Leeches
summary: The vampires, as the Garou see them.

claims.text: Leeches infest every city in Europe and hold great sway over human affairs.
In the Impergium humans turned to the undead for help, and the descendants of those beings still lurk.
Being undying, they plan for the long term; a beaten vampire may return.
Leeches have worked their way into the Church and the Reconquista and led knights to slaughter towns of Kinfolk.

title: The Inquisition
summary: Church hunters who have begun to seek out the Garou.

claims.text: The Children of Gaia fear the inquisitors who seem bent on finding and destroying the Garou, and ask who set them on that trail.

title: Ireland
summary: The land where the Fianna rule among the Garou.

claims.text: In Ireland the Fianna live as their ancestors did, in magical caerns where faerie glamour and spirit gifts mingle.
Many Fianna are better known for song and drink than for battle.
